stories.title: What is the Notre Dame Cathedral?
stories.snippet:
Notre Dame Cathedral is a medieval Catholic cathedral located on the 
eastern end of Île de la Cité in Paris (small island in the Seine River). 
According to historians, Notre Dame de Paris was built on the ruins of 
earlier religious sites: a Roman temple dedicated to Jupiter and an early 
Christian Romanesque basilica.

stories.title: Has Notre Dame reopened?
stories.snippet:
France's iconic Notre Dame Cathedral is formally reopening its doors on 
Saturday for the first time since a devastating fire nearly destroyed the 
861-year-old landmark in 2019.

stories.title: How to visit Notre Dame?
stories.snippet:
Space is first come, first serve for attending Mass. A 10 euro fee is 
required for those who'd like to visit the Notre Dame treasury, which is 
considered a museum. You can make the purchase on-site. Alternatively, you 
can sign up for a free guided tour of the exterior with the volunteer 
organization CASA.
